stories.title: 15-cell metric aggregator + FP multiplier
acceptanceCriteria: dataset_registry.py adds `forensic_combined(per_cell: dict[str, float], clean_fp: int, max_allowed: int, floor: float = 0.01) -> dict` that computes geometric mean of the 15 cells (floored) × (1 - clean_fp/max_allowed) clamped to [0, 1]
Cell names follow convention `<dataset>_t<tier>_<regime>` for 12 spliced cells and `<dataset>_clean_score` for 3 clean cells
Returns dict with keys: combined, combined_gm_cells, fp_multiplier, per_cell, n_cells_included

Inline __main__ test: for 15 synthetic cells all at 0.5 + 0 clean_fp, combined == 0.5. For one cell at 0.01 + others at 0.5, combined drops below 0.38 (demonstrating GM penalty). For 5 clean_fp / max_allowed=15, fp_multiplier == 0.667.
Does NOT replace the existing aggregate_combined — it sits alongside as the forensic-specific aggregator

stories.title: Feature extraction module features.py (~75 dims per candidate)
stories.note: Shipped: features.py 818 lines, 75 dims, 300ms/1000 calls, DIAG INFO for ENF absent + PCA self-fit exercised
acceptanceCriteria: New features.py at repo root exports `extract_features(audio, sr, t_sec, chunk_ctx=None) -> dict[str, float]` returning ~75 named features

Feature categories covered: 4 DSP scores, 13 MFCC pre/post deltas, 6 spectral summary deltas, 6 noise-floor color features, 8 pitch/voicing, 6 energy/ZCR, 3 boundary-region, 20 mel-PCA-tail, 5 ENF (50/60Hz hum continuity), 4 codec-artifact (frame-alignment + quant-residual)

ENF block (5 dims): hum-band freq mean pre/post, freq delta, phase continuity across t, band SNR. Auto-detects 50Hz vs 60Hz from the stronger harmonic; if both absent, emits zeros + DIAG INFO (not an error).

Codec-artifact block (4 dims): frame-alignment offset consistency near t (MP3 576-sample / AAC 1024-sample grids), quantization-residual energy pre, post, double-compression quantization score. Graceful when source is WAV-only (values reduce to residual jitter; no crash).
Every feature has a documented name; `extract_features` also exports FEATURE_NAMES list for SHAP labeling
Idempotent: same (audio, sr, t) produces identical output vector
Performance: 1000 calls on a cached chunk_ctx complete in <2s on laptop CPU (budget for dense scanning)
Integration: ml_eval or a training script can call it to produce a feature matrix
Note: PCA fit for mel tail and ENF base-frequency estimate pre-loaded from training-time fit files if present; self-fit fallback if not

stories.title: SHAP feature-importance rollup injected into autoresearch prompt
stories.note: scripts/shap_rollup.py reads reports/<sha>/<domain>/*.json, sums |shap| per feature across last 5 keeps, writes .omc/shap_rollup.json. run_autoresearch.sh regenerates rollup per iteration and injects compact 'TOP PREDICTIVE FEATURES' block (top-6 per domain). Rollup runs in 0.07s. Empty-history and n<=0 edge cases handled.
acceptanceCriteria: New script scripts/shap_rollup.py reads reports/<sha>/<group>/*.json across the last N (default 5) 'keep' commits from results.tsv and computes per-domain top-10 features by sum of |shap| across all detections in those commits

Rollup output is written deterministically to .omc/shap_rollup.json with keys: generated_at (ISO), keeps_considered (list of short shas), per_domain (dict of domain_id -> list of {name, sum_abs_shap, mean_value, n_detections, rank})

run_autoresearch.sh regenerates .omc/shap_rollup.json once per iteration (after keep/discard is logged, before next claude subprocess starts) and injects a 'TOP PREDICTIVE FEATURES (rolling sum_|shap| over last 5 keeps, per domain)' block into the claude prompt

Rollup script degrades gracefully: if fewer than N keeps exist in results.tsv, use what's available; if zero keeps, write empty per_domain={} and the wrapper's prompt block reads '(not enough history yet)'
Rollup script completes in <5s on the current reports/ tree (187 commits × up to ~110 files each)
A unit-style sanity run `uv run python scripts/shap_rollup.py --keeps 3 --stdout` prints a JSON object matching the schema above to stdout without writing to disk

stories.title: Deep orphan detection: scan history, not just HEAD
stories.note: _detect_deep_orphans() walks last 20 commits, flags hypothesis: with no paired baseline: and no results.tsv row. Pre-TSV-tracker commits filtered via awk cutoff on earliest tracked SHA. Warn-only (no auto-revert). Standalone-callable via `source run_autoresearch.sh`. False-positive guard is structural: only `hypothesis:` subjects match.
acceptanceCriteria: run_autoresearch.sh's orphan-detection step looks back up to N=20 commits (not just HEAD) for any 'hypothesis: …' commit that is NOT followed within 3 commits by a 'baseline: …' commit on the same branch AND does NOT appear in results.tsv as discard/keep/verify-fail
When such an orphan is found, wrapper logs a structured '.omc/autoresearch.log' entry with the orphan SHA, subject, and the detection reason (no paired baseline, not in results.tsv)

Wrapper DOES NOT auto-revert deep orphans (too dangerous — could discard human-authored commits like baseline-restore). Instead it writes a warning and continues. Only HEAD-level orphans (existing behavior) still auto-revert.

Unit-ish check: a shell helper function _detect_deep_orphans() is extracted and callable standalone; `bash -c 'source run_autoresearch.sh; _detect_deep_orphans 20'` prints zero or more warning lines to stderr and returns 0

False-positive guard: commits whose subject is 'baseline-restore:' or 'chore:' or 'refactor:' or 'feat:' or 'fix:' or 'test:' or 'docs:' are NEVER flagged (they're human-authored maintenance, not autoresearch hypotheses)

stories.title: Per-phase iteration timing instrumentation
stories.note: Helpers: _phase_start / _phase_end / _phase_skip / _iter_summary / _reset_iter_timers using bash $SECONDS (<1ms per call). Instrumented: claude (hypothesis form), retrain (conditional on features.py drift), eval (evaluate.py + parse), verify (strict-improvement path only), note (_append_note). Each outcome branch (keep/discard/verify-fail × 3 paths) emits ITER_SUMMARY. scripts/phase_stats.py parses PHASE + ITER_SUMMARY lines, computes median + p95 across trailing N iterations. Synthetic smoke test: correct 1s/2s timings, skipped phases show `-`, all outcome routes emit summary.
acceptanceCriteria: Wrapper emits explicit `PHASE <name>: Ns` log lines for each of: claude (hypothesis formation), retrain (auto-retrain when features.py drift), eval (evaluate.py + RESULTS_TSV parse), verify (verify_agent structural checks — strict-improvement path only), note (_append_note + notebook digest). Phases that were skipped for this iteration print `-` in the summary.

Per-iteration summary line `ITER_SUMMARY iter=<short_sha> status=<keep|discard|verify-fail> total=<N>s claude=<N|->s retrain=<N|->s eval=<N|->s verify=<N|->s note=<N|->s` emitted once per iteration at each outcome branch (keep, discard, verify-fail, parse-fail, retrain-fail, eval-crash).

Per-phase helpers `_phase_start <name>` and `_phase_end <name>` + `_phase_skip <name>` + `_iter_summary <sha> <status>` + `_reset_iter_timers` defined near the top of run_autoresearch.sh. Each uses only bash `$SECONDS` (no date-command overhead) for <100ms impact per call site.

New scripts/phase_stats.py parses `PHASE` + `ITER_SUMMARY` lines from .omc/autoresearch.log, computes per-phase median + p95 across trailing N (default 20) iterations, prints a compact table. Runs in <1s. Graceful fallback on missing data.
`scripts/phase_stats.py --stdout` sanity run prints a summary of current timing distribution without writing to disk.

No collateral damage: ITER_SUMMARY + PHASE lines sit in autoresearch.log only; no new gitignored state files; no collision with guard-stash paths; clean-iteration path still prints the existing log lines plus the new timing ones (purely additive).
All new reset paths still use `_guarded_reset` (no new `git reset --hard` sites).
Regression: `bash -n run_autoresearch.sh` passes; `uv run python scripts/phase_stats.py` prints either a stats table or `(no iteration summaries yet)` on a fresh log.
